For t<1/2, the number f(t) is negative real, so the proposed identity would force
ϕ(t)∈(2Z+1)π.
(6)
Continuity on the connected interval [0,1/2) makes ϕ equal to one fixed odd multiple of π there. For t>1/2, the number f(t) is positive real, so ϕ must instead equal one fixed even multiple of π. These two constants cannot agree, and their one-sided limits at 1/2 therefore contradict continuity. The fact that f(1/2)=0 removes the phase condition at that one point but does not repair the discontinuity.
Now let g:[0,1]→C∖{0} and put h=g/∣g∣. This is a continuous path in the unit circle. The exponential map θ↦eiθ is a covering map, so the path lifting theorem supplies a continuous lift θ:[0,1]→R after one value of θ(0) is chosen. Hence
g(t)=∣g(t)∣eiθ(t).
(7)
One can obtain the same lift directly from the allowed special case: by uniform continuity, subdivide [0,1] so that on each subinterval h(t)/h(tj​) lies in the right half-plane, choose its continuous local argument there, and add a multiple of 2π to match the preceding endpoint.
If θ and θ are two such phases, then
2πθ(t)−θ(t)​∈Z.
(8)
This integer-valued function is continuous and hence constant. Therefore
r(g)=θ(1)−θ(0)
(9)
does not depend on the chosen lift.
For u(t)=g(t2), the phase θ(t2) gives
r(u)=r(g)​.
(10)
For v(t)=g(t)2, the phase 2θ(t) gives
r(v)=2r(g)​.
(11)
Finally, take
g1​(t)=1,g2​(t)=e2πit.
(12)
They have the same two endpoints, but r(g1​)=0 and r(g2​)=2π. This endpoint discrepancy records the winding number of the closed path.

3K (Coding and Cryptography)

Words: 175 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 175
3K OurBigBook.com
A general binary feedback shift register of length d has state
(xn​,xn+1​,…,xn+d−1​)∈F2d​
(13)
and a feedback function F:F2d​→F2​. One update outputs the oldest bit, shifts the state, and inserts
xn+d​=F(xn​,…,xn+d−1​).
(14)
The initial fill is (x0​,…,xd−1​). It is a linear-feedback shift register when
F(z0​,…,zd−1​)=c0​z0​+⋯+cd−1​zd−1​
(15)
for fixed ci​∈F2​.
The Berlekamp-Massey algorithm reads an intercepted sequence from left to right while maintaining the shortest connection polynomial that reproduces the prefix. At each new symbol it computes the discrepancy between the observed bit and that predicted by the current recurrence. A zero discrepancy leaves the polynomial unchanged; a nonzero discrepancy adds a suitably shifted copy of the connection polynomial saved at the previous increase in linear complexity. After at least twice the unknown register length, it recovers the shortest recurrence, after which the entire keystream can be predicted.
Applying those discrepancy updates to
1,1,0,0,1,0,1,1
(16)
returns the connection polynomial
C(D)=1+D2+D3​.
(17)
Equivalently, the sequence obeys
xn​=xn−2​+xn−3​(mod2)(n≥3)​.
(18)
Indeed this predicts successively 0,1,0,1,1. No recurrence of length one or two fits the prefix, so its linear complexity is three.

4I OurBigBook.com
A context-free grammar is in Chomsky normal form when every production has one of the forms
A→BC,A→a,
(19)
where A,B,C are nonterminals and a is a terminal. One may additionally allow S→ϵ when the empty word belongs to the language, usually with the restriction that the start symbol does not occur on a right-hand side.
An ϵ-production has the form A→ϵ. A unit production has the form A→B for nonterminals A,B.
In G1​, the productions for T give
LG1​​(T)={c}{a,b}∗.
(20)
Consequently
L(G1​)={ϵ}∪{a,b}c{a,b}∗a.
(21)
In G2​, X and Y generate a and b, while T→TX∣TY∣c again gives
LG2​​(T)={c}{a,b}∗.
(22)
Since Z→TX, the two start productions S→XZ∣YZ generate exactly
L(G2​)={a,b}c{a,b}∗a.
(23)
Thus
L(G2​)=L(G1​)∖{ϵ}​.
(24)
Every production of G2​ has the required binary-nonterminal or single-terminal form, so G2​ is the Chomsky-normal-form grammar for the nonempty part of L(G1​).

5J OurBigBook.com
Writing Yi​=medvi​, Li​=lstati​, and Ai​=agei​, the fitted normal linear model is
Yi​=β0​+β1​Li​+β2​Ai​+β3​Li​Ai​+εi​,εi​∼iidN(0,σ2).
(25)
The R formula lstat * age includes both main effects and their interaction term.
Three notable features are:
  • The fitted model is highly significant overall: its F statistic is 209.3 on (3,502) degrees of freedom with p<2.2×10−16. Its R2=0.5557, however, means that about 44% of the observed response variation remains unexplained, and the residual standard deviation is about 6.15 house-value units.
  • At fixed age, the fitted slope with respect to lstat is
    −1.3921+0.004156A.
    (26)
    The large negative main coefficient is strongly significant. The positive interaction is significant at the 5% level (p=0.0252), indicating that this negative association becomes slightly weaker for older housing tracts.
  • The age main-effect estimate is essentially zero with p=0.9711, but it is the age effect specifically at L=0 and should not be interpreted separately from the significant interaction. The diagnostic plots also show curved residual structure, increasing spread, a heavy upper tail with observations 215, 372, and 373, and substantial influence from observation 215. These features cast doubt on linearity, constant variance, and Gaussian residual assumptions.

Words: 193 Articles: 1

Solution

Words: 193
7E OurBigBook.com
The Papperitz symbol
P⎩⎨⎧​z1​α1​β1​​z2​α2​β2​​z3​α3​β3​​⎭⎬⎫​
(40)
describes the two-dimensional solution space of a second-order homogeneous Fuchsian differential equation on the Riemann sphere with exactly three regular singular points z1​,z2​,z3​. Near zi​, its two independent Frobenius behaviours are locally
(z−zi​)αi​and(z−zi​)βi​,
(41)
subject to logarithmic modifications in resonant cases. The six characteristic exponents obey the Fuchs relation
∑i=13​(αi​+βi​)=1.
(42)
For the Gauss hypergeometric equation, the exponents at infinity are a and b. Put w=z−1. Transforming the Papperitz symbol from z to w shows that
ya​(z)=z−aF(a,1+a−c;1+a−b;z−1)
(43)
and
yb​(z)=z−bF(b,1+b−c;1+b−a;z−1)
(44)
are local solutions near z=∞, with respective leading behaviours z−a and z−b. When a−b∈/Z, these behaviours are distinct and the two solutions are linearly independent. They therefore form a basis of the solution space on any simply connected common domain with compatible branch choices.
The solution F(a,b;c;z) normalized at zero can be analytically continued into that domain. Since it solves the same second-order equation, it must be a constant linear combination of the basis at infinity:
F(a,b;c;z)=Az−aF(a,1+a−c;1+a−b;z−1)+Bz−bF(b,1+b−c;1+b−a;z−1)​.
(45)
The constants depend on a,b,c and the branch convention, but not on z. This is the hypergeometric connection formula at infinity.

Taking downward distance as positive, the Lagrangian is
L=21​(3m)z˙12​+21​(2m)z˙22​−2k​(z1​−l)2−2k​(z2​−z1​−l)2+3mgz1​+2mgz2​​.
(46)
At equilibrium the lower spring supports only the lower mass, while the upper spring supports both masses:
k(z2​−z1​−l)=2mg,k(z1​−l)=5mg.
(47)
Hence
z1(0)​=l+k5mg​,z2(0)​=2l+k7mg​​.
(48)
Let qi​=zi​−zi(0)​. The linear terms cancel by the equilibrium equations, and the quadratic Lagrangian is
L=21​q˙​TTq˙​−21​qTVq+constant,
(49)
with the small-oscillation mass and stiffness matrices
T=m(30​02​),V=k(2−1​−11​)​.
(50)
The generalized eigenvalue problem for small oscillations is
(V−ω2T)a=0.
(51)
Its characteristic equation is
det(V−ω2T)=k2−7kmω2+6m2ω4=0,
(52)
so
ω1​=6mk​​,ω2​=mk​​​.
(53)
Corresponding displacement eigenvectors are
a1​=(2,3)T,a2​=(1,−1)T​.
(54)
They are not orthogonal in the ordinary Euclidean inner product. They are orthogonal in the kinetic-energy, or mass-matrix, inner product:
a1T​Ta2​=(2,3)m(30​02​)(−11​)=0​.
(55)
This is mass-matrix orthogonality of normal modes.

9A (Cosmology)

Words: 175 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 175
9A OurBigBook.com
The constant R is the curvature radius of the closed spatial slices when a=1; at general scale factor their curvature radius is Ra and their scalar curvature is 6/(R2a2).
The cosmological perfect-fluid continuity equation is
ρ˙​+3aa˙​(ρ+P)=0.
(56)
During expansion, a˙>0, and therefore
dtd​(ρa3)=−3Pa2a˙≤0.
(57)
If C=ρ(t0​)a(t0​)3, then throughout the later expanding phase
ρa3≤C.
(58)
Multiplying the Friedmann equation by a2 gives
a˙2=3c28πG​ρa2−R2c2​≤3c2a8πGC​−R2c2​.
(59)
The right-hand side is negative once
a>3c48πGCR2​,
(60)
which is impossible because a˙2≥0. Thus the scale factor cannot grow without bound.
In fact the expanding phase ends in finite time. Combining the Friedmann and continuity equations yields the Friedmann acceleration equation
aa¨​=−3c24πG​(ρ+3P)<0.
(61)
The curvature term in the first Friedmann equation also implies
ρ≥8πGR2a23c4​.
(62)
While a remains below the finite bound just found, a¨ is bounded above by a strictly negative constant. Hence a˙ reaches zero after finite time: the closed universe attains a maximum size and cannot expand forever. This is recollapse of a closed Friedmann universe with nonnegative pressure.

where H is the Hadamard gate. For a computational-basis string z, define the phase reflection
Iz​=I−2∣z⟩⟨z∣.

Thus I0​ changes the sign of ∣0n⟩, while Ix0​​ changes the sign of the marked state.
Conjugating I0​ by Hn​ reflects in the hyperplane perpendicular to ∣s⟩, so
−Hn​I0​Hn​=2∣s⟩⟨s∣−I
(65)
is the Grover diffusion operator, the reflection about ∣s⟩. The Grover iteration operator
Q=(2∣s⟩⟨s∣−I)Ix0​​

sinθ=N​1​.

UI​Uf​∣x⟩∣y⟩={∣x⟩∣y⟩,∣x⟩∣y⊕a⟩,​x=x0​,x=x0​.​

Prepare the answer register as
∣0⟩⊗(n−1)∣−⟩,∣−⟩=2​∣0⟩−∣1⟩​.
(71)
Since X∣−⟩=−∣−⟩, quantum phase kickback gives, for an arbitrary search-register state,
(UI​Uf​)∣x⟩∣0n−1⟩∣−⟩=(−1)[x=x0​]∣x⟩∣0n−1⟩∣−⟩.

Ix0​​=I−2∣x0​⟩⟨x0​∣​.

The Gershgorin circle theorem states that every eigenvalue λ of a complex matrix A=(aij​) lies in at least one disk
∣λ−aii​∣≤j=i∑​∣aij​∣​.
(420)
To prove it, choose a nonzero eigenvector x for λ and an index i such that ∣xi​∣=maxj​∣xj​∣>0. The ith component of Ax=λx gives
(λ−aii​)xi​=∑j=i​aij​xj​.
(421)
Taking absolute values and using ∣xj​∣≤∣xi​∣ yields
∣λ−aii​∣∣xi​∣≤∑j=i​∣aij​∣∣xj​∣≤∣xi​∣∑j=i​∣aij​∣.
(422)
Division by ∣xi​∣ proves the theorem.

Let Lh​ be the spatial matrix, so the forward Euler method is
Un+1=(I+kLh​)Un.
(427)
The conservative use of shared edge coefficients makes Lh​ a real symmetric matrix. In an interior row, put s=α+β+γ+δ<4amax​. Its diagonal entry is −s/h2, and the sum of the absolute off-diagonal entries is s/h2. Boundary rows have no larger disk because homogeneous Dirichlet data remove some unknown neighbors.
The Gershgorin circle theorem and symmetry therefore place every eigenvalue of Lh​ in
[−h22s​,0]⊆[−h28amax​​,0].
(428)
If μ=k/h2, each amplification eigenvalue is 1+kλ. It lies in [−1,1] whenever
1−8μamax​≥−1,
(429)
or
0<μ≤4amax​1​​.
(430)
Since the amplification matrix is symmetric, bounding all its eigenvalues in modulus by one bounds its discrete Euclidean operator norm by one. This proves the stated stability condition and is the Gershgorin stability bound for a variable-coefficient diffusion stencil.
